content: Symptoms of bronchiectasis include a chronic productive cough, wheezing, shortness of breath, and recurrent infections of the lower respiratory tract. Long-acting bronchodilators are increasingly being used in the treatment of individuals with this condition. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of long-acting bronchodilators in managing bronchiectasis that is not caused by cystic fibrosis. To achieve this, a search was conducted using the Cochrane Airways Group Specialised Register of bronchiectasis trials. The most recent search was performed in August 2010. The selection criteria included randomized controlled trials, regardless of whether they were blinded or unblinded. The data from the search results were reviewed and assessed based on pre-specified criteria. However, no randomized controlled trials were identified that investigated the effectiveness of long-acting bronchodilator therapy in the management of bronchiectasis. An updated search conducted in August 2010 also failed to identify any new studies. The authors concluded that further research is necessary to determine whether long-acting bronchodilators play a role in the management of individuals with bronchiectasis.
